text:
maria: heads up — our GHAS pipeline started failing scans on the nightly run around 01:40 UTC, looks related to scanner cache decryption.
cheng: ugh, did KMS rotate yesterday? :eyes:
ops-bot: deploy log: ERROR: failed to decrypt cache blob: kms.Decrypt permission_denied for key alias/redwood-scanner-2026
sam: confirmed, key rotation happened during the maintenance window at 01:15. we pushed new key but IAM role for runner wasn't updated.
maria: that would explain intermittent failures for Trivy and Snyk adapters — they read cached layer metadata and then try to decrypt signatures.
security-qa: impact? are scans completely blocked or falling back to full rescan?
maria: GHAS shows job status as "failed"; Snyk adapter retries but then times out (we see ~30% of jobs stuck). Trivy CLI in our wrapper does full fetch if cache unreadable, but GHAS doesn't have that fallback.
cheng: quick mitigation: add temporary policy granting kms:Decrypt to ghas-runner-role for the new key alias, then we can re-run the backlog. I'll open a short-lived IAM change and notify infra.
sam: FYI that policy needs an approval (security review). Can we scope it to the key ARN and the runner role only? we should avoid broad grants.
maria: yes scope to arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-rotated and principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ghas-runner
ops-bot: created issue #4321: "ghas-runner kms decrypt permission for rotated scanner key" — link: https://rwd/internal/4321
security-qa: should we add a suppression for known cache-decrypt failures to avoid noise in vuln triage dashboards? we don't want recurring false positives while infra fixes perms.
cheng: we can add a short suppression rule in our scanner orchestration that marks failures with `kms.Decrypt` as infra-level and not create vuln alerts. but keep logs and create pager if >10% of jobs fail in an hour.
maria: agree. suppression rule snippet I tested locally:
```
- matcher: "kms.Decrypt"
  action: suppress
  scope: pipeline
  ttl: 2h
  notify_threshold: 10%
```
sam: that looks fine, but ensure GHAS job annotations still surface to compliance audit logs — suppression shouldn't wipe audit trails.
maria: suppression will only silence alert creation in our vuln-triage pipeline; GHAS web UI and raw job logs remain untouched.
security-qa: after perms fix + suppression, we should re-run affected commits. also need to document in incident log: root cause (key rotation + missing role update), mitigation, and follow-up (automate role-key mapping on rotation).
cheng: follow-up: add a small lambda to auto-update runner role trust or a runbook step in KMS rotation playbook. I'll draft PR.
maria: timeline: cheng to apply IAM change now, ops to re-run GHAS backlog, sam to approve the IAM scope in parallel, security-qa to deploy suppression rule, and I'll monitor the triage dashboard.
ops-bot: action items assigned: cheng -> IAM patch, security-qa -> suppression deploy, sam -> IAM approval, maria -> monitor. ETA 30m.
sam: approved the scoped policy via TFC; cheng you can apply.
cheng: applied. rerunning the ghast-nightly job now.
ops-bot: ghast-nightly #482 rerun queued, will post status.
ops-bot: ghast-nightly #482 completed: SUCCESS. scan artifacts uploaded.
maria: nice. I'm seeing reduced failure rate on the dashboard. still a few legacy blobs with old key alias that need manual re-encryption.
security-qa: filing a follow-up ticket to re-encrypt older cache blobs and to add a check to rotation playbook. ticket #4322.
maria: also adding a short note to the runbook: "When rotating KMS keys used by scanners, update runner IAM role and invalidate old cache or re-encrypt blobs. If failures occur, suppress kms.Decrypt errors for up to 2h and escalate if >10% jobs fail." 
sam: thanks folks — good triage. we should also add an audit entry for compliance: who changed IAM and why.
maria: will add to incident log and ping compliance. :white_check_mark:
